claim: The direct Penang-Langkawi passenger ferry stopped in 2020 and has not restarted; historically RM70, 2.5-3 hours.
quote: There was a ferry until 2020 but it became a victim of the pandemic... The journey takes between 2 1/2 hours and 3 hours... Fares were RM70 per passenger.

claim: With no direct ferry, most travellers fly Penang to Langkawi or go via a mainland Kedah/Perlis jetty.
quote: How to get from Penang to Langkawi: the easy way and the not-so-easy way

claim: AirAsia and others fly KUL-Langkawi direct in about 1 hour, fares from roughly USD 18 / RM 73 one-way.
quote: The Kuala Lumpur to Langkawi flight takes only around 1 hour... Flights from Kuala Lumpur Airport to Langkawi on AirAsia start from $18.

claim: Mainland ferries to Langkawi run from Kuala Perlis and Kuala Kedah, arriving at Kuah Jetty; Telaga Harbour is the second island port.
quote: Ferries to Langkawi depart from two ports in Kedah and Perlis: Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis... arrive at Kuah Jetty.

claim: Kuala Perlis to Langkawi ferry takes about 1h15 and costs from RM35 one-way; ro-ro ferries carry vehicles.
quote: The ferry takes only 1 hour 15 minutes... Ferry ticket prices start from RM 35 for a one-way trip... carrying cars, motorcycles, and even buses.

claim: Kuala Kedah to Langkawi ferry takes about 1h45 and costs around RM23 adult, running roughly every 1-1.5 hours from 7am to 7pm.
quote: Travel time: 1 hour 45 minutes... One way tickets on these ferries cost 23 MYR for Adults... Ferries run from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM approximately every 1-1.5 hours.

claim: Reaching the Perhentians from Langkawi is multi-leg: ferry to a mainland jetty plus a long bus/taxi to Kuala Besut, or fly via KL/Penang to Kota Bharu (3h+, ~RM196) then overland to the Kuala Besut boat.
quote: Flying from Langkawi International Airport to Kota Bharu, even with a stopover in Kuala Lumpur, takes just over 3 hours and costs around RM 196... take a ferry from Kuah in Langkawi to Kuala Perlis, then take a night bus from Kuala Perlis to Kuala Besut.

claim: Langkawi-Koh Lipe ferry crosses in about 90 minutes from Telaga Harbour or Kuah Jetty, RM152-160 one-way, plus ~1h Thai immigration and 30min Malaysian; day trips possible but consume most of the day.
quote: The ferry journey takes approximately 90 minutes, plus immigration processing (roughly 1 hour in Thailand, 30 minutes in Malaysia)... Adult RM 152-160 one-way... day trips are feasible... would consume most of a single day.

claim: The Langkawi-Koh Lipe ferry runs only in season, roughly late October through early June, closing June-September for the monsoon.
quote: Season Opening Oct 2025 - May 2026

claim: Car hire from RM50/day at the airport (RM120 at Cenang), scooters from RM30-50/day, and airport taxis use fixed-price coupons (~RM12 within a beach area, RM16+ between beaches).
quote: At the airport, car rental starts from 50 ringgit... Motorbike rentals at the airport start from 30 ringgit per day... a short taxi ride within a single area/beach costs around 12 ringgit, while between beaches it's from 16 ringgit.

claim: Grab e-hailing does operate in Langkawi and is cheaper than coupon taxis, but driver supply is thin so waits can be long.
quote: Does Langkawi Have Grab? Here's What Every Traveller Should Know Before Visiting

claim: Langkawi has no public transport, so a rental car, scooter, or e-hailing/taxi is required; car rental is the standard choice.
quote: Getting Around Langkawi: Rental Car, Scooters or Grab?

claim: The classic island-hopping boat tour is about RM50/pax for a 3-4 hour cruise covering Dayang Bunting lake, eagle feeding and Beras Basah, with morning (9am-1pm) and afternoon (2-6pm) sessions.
quote: Price per person is reasonable RM50... a relaxing 3 to 4-hour cruise... 2 sessions per day: morning from 9am till 1pm and 2pm till 6pm.

claim: Island-hopping stops at Dayang Bunting (Pregnant Maiden Lake), Singa Besar for eagle watching and Beras Basah beach; lake entry is RM6 for non-Malaysians.
quote: visit Dayang Bunting Island (Pregnant Maiden Lake), Singa Besar Island for eagle watching, and Beras Basah Island... entrance fee to Tasik Dayang Bunting... RM6 per person for non-Malaysian passport holders.

claim: Pulau Payar snorkelling packages start around RM125/pax including gear, life jacket, ferry and lunch; full-day diving options run higher.
quote: Langkawi snorkeling packages start from RM125 per person, which includes equipment for snorkeling, life jacket, ferry, and a lunch.

claim: Pulau Payar Marine Park is ~30km/45min south of Kuah by speedboat, a full-day (roughly 9am-3pm) trip; it closes Tuesdays and Wednesdays and shuts entirely March 1-May 31 for conservation.
quote: Pulau Payar is just 30km south of the main island and takes about 45 minutes from the Kuah jetty point... closed every Tuesday and Wednesday for conservation, and closed from March 1 to May 31 every year.

claim: Kilim Geoforest Park is the official UNESCO-listed mangrove area on Langkawi's northeast, toured by boat past limestone karst, caves and eagle-feeding spots.
quote: Kilim Mangrove Tour - The Official Park Manager of Kilim Geoforest Park

claim: Kilim mangrove boat tours start around RM33/pax shared (RM270 for a private 8-seater); sharing tours are typically 3-4 hours.
quote: Langkawi Mangrove Tour 2026 | Private Boat from RM33/Pax... RM270 for a private eight-seater boat.

claim: Shared Kilim mangrove tours run ~RM65/pax (RM77 with a chicken-rice set) over about 3 hours, with bat-cave entry RM2 extra.
quote: Sharing Boat Tours: RM65 per person... or RM77 per person (including Fried Chicken Rice Set)... The Bat Cave entry costs RM2 per person.

claim: Dry season Nov-Mar is best; the wettest monsoon months are September-October, when rain is heaviest and ferries/sea trips are most affected.
quote: November to March is the best time to visit Langkawi... September to October is the wettest period... avoid the worst of the Langkawi monsoon season which occurs during September and October.

claim: In 2026 one euro buys roughly RM4.7 (range ~4.60-4.77), so RM amounts divide by about 4.7 for EUR.
quote: The average EUR/MYR exchange rate for 2026 is 4.6972 Malaysian Ringgits per Euro.
